title: normalize_team strips the -UF state suffix, so clubs differing only by state collapse in standings/queries
evidence: soccer_mcp.py:35 re.sub(r'\s*[-–—]\s*[A-Z]{2}\s*$', ...) reduces both 'Atletico-MG' and 'Atletico-PR' to 'atletico' (verified); standings() keys on normalize_team(side) at soccer_mcp.py:215. In Brasileirao_Matches.csv both Atlético clubs are spelled 'Atletico-XX' (no h) and WOULD merge; 2019 escapes only because that file is skipped (historical_cutoff, soccer_mcp.py:90-101) and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv spells them 'Atlético-MG' vs 'Athletico-PR' (→ atletico vs athletico).
suggestion: Do not strip the -UF suffix when it disambiguates distinct clubs; key standings on a canonical club id, or keep the suffix for the Atlético/Athletico pair.

title: Recorded factual gate reported 19/20 clubs for 2019, but archived code+data reproduces 20 distinct rows
evidence: _factual.json note: 'got 19 of 20 (1 Atlético/Athletico row(s), expected 2)' → factual_accuracy=0.5. Re-running db.standings(2019) on the archived workspace yields 20 rows, Flamengo 90pts P38, with Atlético-MG (48pts) and Athletico-PR (64pts) as SEPARATE rows. The gate's 19 stems from its canonical-club tally collapsing the two output rows, not from a truncated/merged standings table.
suggestion: Informational only — factual_accuracy is a separate scorer and is not re-scored here; the standings tool itself returns all 20 clubs for 2019.

title: R9 (season standings computed from matches) is IMPLEMENTED — first evaluator marked it missing in error
evidence: soccer_mcp.py:210-220 standings() accumulates played/W/D/L/points/goals per team from matches_query results and sorts by (points, GD, GF); test_standings_and_aggregates and test_overlapping_brasileirao_sources_are_not_double_counted exercise it (test_soccer_mcp.py:35-49). Nothing is hardcoded, satisfying R9's how_to_verify. The prior evaluation conflated the factual-accuracy Atlético merge with requirement R9.
